newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds dip slightly with Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds dip slightly with Treasuries.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities held their own against Treasuries on Friday as government securities slipped modestly on foreign central bank selling, fixed-income analysts said.
Ginnie Mae pass-throughs outperformed other agency paper much of the day, traders said. "Ginnies did well (and) spreads came in a little," said one trader.
GNMAs may have gotten more looks because they are more liquid than other agency issues, said a trader at a West Coat regional firm. "I have to think it had something to do with liquity," she said.
Most transactions involved small bundles of securities, with sellers outnumbering buyers, traders said. "It was a lot of odd lots and trading up," said one.
By late afternoon, Ginnie Mae 30-year 8.0 percent coupons were off 5/32 at 100-02/32, yielding 120 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Thirty-year Fannie Mae 7.5 percents were off 3/32 at 99-01/32, and comparable Freddie Macs had fallen 2/32 to 99-05/32.
The 10-year note was off 3/32 to yield 6.67 percent in late trading.
